_comment: Canonical fixture corpus for the Deployment Dashboard. Two complementary sections:
slots[]   - the original 6-box-state corpus (Phase 1). Drives matrix tests + E2E.
Every event now carries a stable 'deployment_id' (Phase 2 SAD update).
These slots intentionally OMIT 'parent_deployments' so the topology
derivation falls back to the correlation attribute (default: 'version'),
keeping the Phase 1 assertions stable.
topology[] - Phase 2 topology corpus. Three independent services exercising the
three derivation paths from SAD §5 'Topology Derivation':
* topo-explicit  - explicit parent_deployments chain (source='explicit')
* topo-correlated - no parents, shared version (source='correlated')
* topo-mixed     - some events explicit, some correlated; explicit
wins on (from,to) overlap per the Merge pass.
Each topology service uses an actor outside 'qa.bot' (qa.bot-topo)
so cleanup by actor marker still purges them.
Derived from docs/ui/deployment-dashboard.html and
docs/deployment-dashboard-architecture.md §4 (FR-13), §5 (Data Model + Topology
Derivation), §7 (API Contract - POST validation, Matrix response shape).
deployment_id values are CI/CD-side identifiers (SAD §5 deployments table). They are
stable across seed re-runs, so a re-seed reuses the same id and the Write API
returns 409 Conflict for every event after the first run - the matrix view is
still deterministic because the original rows are unchanged.
ref / sha (Phase 2, FR-05): events MAY carry the two optional source-identifier
fields. Per SAD §10 Decision #10, both are nullable, unconstrained strings - this
cycle introduces them additively, no validation. The corpus exercises every
combination so consumers across functional, SSE, and e2e suites can assert the
omit-or-null tolerance rule (SAD §7 'Matrix response shape - per service' field
rules - 'absent and null are equivalent'):
* service-b/dev (success)                              -> both ref + sha
* service-a/dev (running-with-last-success)            -> ref only, both events
* service-c/dev (running-with-prev-failed-and-success) -> sha only on one event
* service-b/qa  (failed-with-last-success)             -> neither (legacy shape)
* service-d/uat (running)                              -> neither (legacy shape)
* service-d/dev (running-with-prev-failed)             -> mixed across history
Topology services topo-explicit / topo-correlated / topo-mixed intentionally
OMIT ref + sha - their concern is the parent DAG, not the source-identifier
wire shape. Two ADDITIONAL topology services exist to exercise the FR-13
'?correlationAttribute=ref|sha' query parameter against fixture data that
actually shares those identifiers across envs:
* topo-ref-correlated  -> no parent_deployments anywhere; every event shares
ref='release/2026.05' across dev/qa/prod. version
and sha are deliberately distinct per event so the
topology builder MUST consult `ref` to derive the
chain. Default correlationAttribute=version would
yield ZERO edges; ?correlationAttribute=ref yields
two correlated edges (dev->qa, qa->prod).
* topo-sha-correlated  -> same construction, correlating on sha='a1b2c3d4e5'.
ref and version differ per event. Default version
-> zero edges; ?correlationAttribute=sha -> two
correlated edges. The sha value is long enough
(10 chars) to exercise the SPA's first-7-char
truncation convention in display.

topology._comment: Pure-explicit chain: dev -> qa -> prod via parent_deployments. Every promotion event names its predecessor by deployment_id. Topology builder must emit two edges with source='explicit'.

Pure-correlated: no parent_deployments anywhere. All three events share version v2.0.0 and land in chronological order (dev -> qa -> prod). The correlation-fallback pass picks the closest-in-time parent per env, emitting (dev->qa) and (qa->prod) with source='correlated'.

Mixed: dev->qa is explicit; qa->prod is left to correlation (shared version v3.0.0). One topology must contain edges with BOTH sources. Per Merge pass, if explicit and correlated both produce the same (from,to) pair, explicit wins - here they don't overlap by construction so we see exactly one of each.

Correlated-by-ref: no parent_deployments; every event has a DISTINCT version + sha but a SHARED ref='release/2026.05'. With the default correlationAttribute=version, the builder finds no matches across envs and emits ZERO edges. With ?correlationAttribute=ref, it emits two correlated edges (dev->qa, qa->prod). Pins the FR-02/FR-13 contract that the read API actually consults `ref` when the per-request hint or per-service override selects it.

Correlated-by-sha: mirror of topo-ref-correlated for the sha axis. Every event has a DISTINCT version + ref but a SHARED sha='a1b2c3d4e5f6' (12 hex chars — long enough that the SPA's first-7-char truncation convention can be exercised end-to-end). With default correlationAttribute=version: ZERO edges. With ?correlationAttribute=sha: two correlated edges (dev->qa, qa->prod). Pins the FR-02/FR-13 contract for sha-correlated topology.
